name: Terengganu
summary_text: In May 2025 the Kuala Terengganu authority installed warning signboards about homosexual practice at several strategic locations in the state, framing homosexuality as 'dirty'; when criticised, state exco member Datuk Wan Sukairi Wan Abdullah confirmed the aim was deliberate — the boards were meant 'to instil hatred towards such acts among the community.' Justice for Sisters and twelve other civil-society organisations demanded removal on 14 May 2025 as a human-rights violation, so the record combines an explicit official statement of hostile intent with a documented civil-society counterweight. Terengganu additionally maintains a Hudud & Qisas Enactment 2002 that is unenforceable because of the federal Act 355 penalty cap — an aspirational legal ceiling the state nonetheless keeps legislating on, having amended its Takzir provisions from December 2022. What a visitor encounters is visible, ongoing, official hostility: signboards at strategic locations broadcasting that the state's stated purpose is to generate hatred; there is no criminalisation of trans status per se (contrast Kelantan), but the atmosphere is explicitly and officially manufactured.

sources.title: Inciting hatred of 'dirty' homosexuality is the point, says Terengganu exco member | The Star
sources.claim_summary: The Star (10 May 2025): Terengganu exco member Wan Shukri defends anti-homosexuality warning signboards — installed near Universiti Malaysia Terengganu and other youth-frequented areas deliberately as a 'constant reminder' — confirming the purpose is to educate away from homosexuality; transgender activist Nisha Ayub condemns the move as institutionalised discrimination.

sources.title: Civil groups urge Terengganu authorities to remove anti-LGBT signboards, warn of human rights violations | Malay Mail
sources.claim_summary: Malay Mail (14 May 2025): Justice for Sisters and 12 other civil-society organisations urge the Kuala Terengganu City Council to immediately remove the anti-LGBT signboards, calling them discriminatory hate speech under international human-rights law and condemning the exco member's defence as inciting hatred.

Legal Dignity analysis (Justice for Sisters / Sisters in Islam, June 2023) of Terengganu's Syariah Criminal Offences Enactment framework: the 2001 Takzir Enactment, its December 2022 amendments, and the Hudud & Qisas Enactment 2002 that is rendered unenforceable by the federal Act 355 penalty ceiling — the documentary basis for the state's shadow capital-punishment code.
